To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in pigs with unstable angina (plaque rupture and microembolization), the increased tumor necrosis alpha (TNF-α) expression is responsible for both the progressive contractile dysfunction as well as the protection against infarct.
in pigs, microembolization-induced myocardial infarction is reduced by increased tumor necrosis-factor-&agr; expression, which, however, also causes progressive contractile dysfunction.

microembolization of the coronary artery with microspheres (ME), which is a common finding in patients with acute coronary syndromes, leads to progressive contractile dysfunction, which can be attenuated by blocking tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-&agr;. In addition, the same ME induces an inflammatory reaction with an increased TNF-&agr;-expression that protects the myocardium against subsequent ischemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of TNF-&agr;, which can be either detrimental or protective in ischemia-reperfusion injury.
the bidirectional role of TNF-&agr;, a proinflammatory cytokine that is increased in patients with unstable anginia, in ME-induced microinfact formation.
the pathogenesis of unstable angina.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TNF-&agr;, in addition to being an important mediator of myocardial dysfunction, is a key regulator of the inflammatory reaction in the myocardium.
TNF-&agr;, which is increased after ME, has a bidirectional effect in the myocardium, resulting in progressive dysfunction but also protection against infarct.
TNF-&agr;, which is released after ME and which causes progressive contractile dysfunction, can also protect the microinfarcted myocardium against infraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TNF-&agr;, which has a bidirectional role in the heart, is not a single factor but rather a multifaceted cytokine that can have a positive effect on the heart when it is expressed in low concentrations.
TNF-&agr;, a mediator of inflammation, has a bidirectional role in the progression of coronary ME-induced microinfarccts.

TNF-&agr;-induced myocardial dysfunction is not a prerequisite for infarction and that the infarct size-reducing effects of TNF-&agr;, which are independent of contractile dysfunction, are abolished by TNF-neutralizing antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TNF-alpha is not only a pro-inflammatory molecule that can cause progressive contractile dysfunction in the heart but also a cardioprotective factor.
TNF-&agr;-mediated microembolization-induced microinfarct is responsible for progressive contractile dysfunction but also for a delayed protection against infraction.
the role of TNF-α in the myocardium is not always detrimental and that it can also be beneficial, depending on the circumstances.
